transcript.text: Good morning, everyone. Thank you for joining today's pre-approval huddle. As you know, the district will administer its required middle-school mathematics assessment on May 14, 2027, and I've asked each of you to review the draft administration plan before I give it final approval. The plan currently calls for digital testing on school tablets, all 26 students testing together in Room 201, one proctor, graphing calculators available throughout the assessment, and completed materials stored in the general records cabinet. I'd like to go around the table and hear any concerns or feedback from each of you before I make my decision. Who would like to start?

transcript.text: I have a concern about the calculator policy in the draft plan. While reviewing the current state mathematics assessment manual this week, I found that calculators may be used only on section 2 of the assessment and must be four-function calculators. The draft plan currently calls for graphing calculators available throughout the assessment, which would violate state guidelines. I have not yet amended the draft plan to reflect this.
transcript.speaker: A3

transcript.text: I need to flag a critical technology concern. My device test found that the 26 assigned tablets cannot run the required secure testing application, and the district cannot obtain compatible devices before May 14. I contacted the assessment vendor, and they confirmed that paper booklets are authorized as an alternative. However, this result has not yet been added to the plan, which currently still calls for digital testing on school tablets.
transcript.speaker: A4

transcript.text: I have a security concern regarding the storage of completed assessment materials. My security review of the state testing agreement, which I completed this week, requires that completed assessment materials be sealed in tamper-evident envelopes and stored in a locked cabinet for exactly 30 calendar days. The draft plan currently calls for completed materials to be stored in the general records cabinet, which does not meet these requirements. I have not yet updated the storage field in the plan to reflect the proper security protocols.
